title: Angle facts
examples: What is the relationship between angles on a straight line?
How do I find an unknown angle when lines are parallel?
Can you show me an example of vertically opposite angles?

explain.say: Today we are learning about important angle facts. We will look at angles on a line, at a point, and when lines are parallel.
Angles on a straight line always add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. Imagine a straight road; the angles on it total one hundred and eighty degrees.
Next, let us look at angles at a point. All angles meeting at a single point always add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. This is called a full circle.
When two lines cross, they form vertically opposite angles. These opposite angles are always equal to each other. For example, if one angle is forty degrees, the opposite angle is also forty degrees.
Finally, consider parallel lines cut by a transversal line. The corresponding angles are equal. This means angles in the same position are the same size.

faq.q: What is the difference between angles on a straight line and angles at a point?
faq.a: Angles on a straight line sum to one hundred and eighty degrees. Angles at a point, which is a full circle, sum to three hundred and sixty degrees.
asks: What is the total of angles on a line?
How many degrees are in a full circle of angles?

faq.q: Do vertically opposite angles always have to be equal?
faq.a: Yes, that is a key rule. When two straight lines intersect, the angles opposite each other are always equal.
asks: If lines cross, are opposite angles the same?
What is the rule for opposite angles?

faq.q: What does it mean if lines are parallel?
faq.a: Parallel lines are lines that run side by side and will never meet, no matter how far they go. Think of train tracks.
asks: How do I know if lines are parallel?
What is the definition of parallel lines?

faq.q: Do corresponding angles have to be equal when lines are parallel?
faq.a: Yes, they must be equal. If you cut two parallel lines with another line, the matching angles in the same position are equal.
asks: What is the rule for the angles when lines are parallel?

faq.q: If I know one angle on a straight line, can I find the other?
faq.a: Yes, you can. You subtract the known angle from one hundred and eighty degrees to find the missing angle.
asks: How do I find the missing angle on a line?
If one angle is 60 degrees, what is the other on the line?

facts: Angles on a straight line add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
Angles at a single point add up to three hundred and sixty degrees.
Vertically opposite angles formed by intersecting lines are equal.
When a transversal cuts parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal.

quiz.say: If an angle is 50 degrees, what is the adjacent angle on a straight line?
quiz.why: Angles on a straight line must total one hundred and eighty degrees, so you subtract 50 from 180.

wrong.0: This is wrong because three hundred sixty degrees is for angles around a point, not on a line.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it suggests the other angle is zero, which is not necessarily true.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the angles must add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, not zero.

quiz.say: Two lines intersect, and one angle is 75 degrees. What is the vertically opposite angle?
quiz.why: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, so the opposite angle must also be seventy-five degrees.

wrong.0: This is wrong because there is no mathematical rule that requires dividing the angle by two.
wrong.1: This is wrong because this calculation finds the adjacent angle, not the opposite angle.
wrong.3: This is wrong because 75 plus 105 equals one hundred and eighty, which is for adjacent angles, not opposite ones.

quiz.say: If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one angle is 110 degrees, what is the corresponding angle?
quiz.why: Corresponding angles are always equal when the lines are parallel, so the other angle is also one hundred and ten degrees.

wrong.0: This is wrong because 110 plus 70 equals one hundred and eighty, which is the rule for adjacent angles.
wrong.1: This is wrong because adding one hundred and eighty degrees makes the angle too large.
wrong.2: This is wrong because this calculation finds the adjacent angle, not the corresponding angle.
